title: Death From Familiarity
body:
15 Minutes w/ The Captains · 2026-09-22

Opens [Matt 11](/bible/matthew/11) · [John 4](/bible/john/4) · [Mark 1](/bible/mark/1) · [Matt 4](/bible/matthew/4) · [Isa 9](/bible/isaiah/9) · [John 7](/bible/john/7) · [John 1](/bible/john/1) · [Matt 21](/bible/matthew/21) · [Mark 6](/bible/mark/6) · [1 Sam 10](/bible/1-samuel/10) · [John 3](/bible/john/3) · [1 Cor 4](/bible/1-corinthians/4) · [John 15](/bible/john/15) · [2 Esdras 9](/bible/2-esdras/9)
## Introduction *[[0:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=15s)]* Today we're going to talk about death from familiarity. This class is to encourage brothers and sisters who are repenting and building not to be discouraged by family, friends and so on, and to be able to see and understand what's going on and how you treat it. That's a big part of this truth. A prophet has no honour in his own country: those who knew Christ, and those who knew Saul before time, were offended because they were familiar with them, and a lot of people in these last days are going to reject this truth for the same reason. ## Scriptures Opened **[Matthew 11:20](/bible/matthew/11#v20)** *[[0:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=37s)]* > [20](/bible/matthew/11#v20) Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not: - Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not.
Reading from a definition of upbraid, on screen *[[0:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=53s)]* > Upbraid is a verb that means to scold, blame, or criticize someone severely for doing something wrong. It involves finding fault with the person and expressing strong disapproval or anger about their actions. - So yeah, this is what the Lord was doing, man. He was scolding them, blaming them, criticizing them, finding fault, expressing strong disapproval. Why? Because the scripture said this is where he did most of his mighty works.
**[Matthew 11:21-24](/bible/matthew/11#v21)** *[[1:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=95s)]* > [21](/bible/matthew/11#v21) Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. > > [22](/bible/matthew/11#v22) But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you. > > [23](/bible/matthew/11#v23) And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. > > [24](/bible/matthew/11#v24) But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee. - These cities right here were where predominantly our people were at. He's saying, listen, if I would have done these same mighty works in Tyre and Sidon and the other nations, they would have already repented. The Lord was scolding them. - If the mighty works done in thee had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day: I wouldn't even have destroyed Sodom if I had done the mighty works there that I did within you, that you saw. - We know what happened with Sodom and Gomorrah: fire and brimstone. So for him to make a statement saying it's going to be more tolerable for Sodom than for you, the Lord was scolding these different lands right here. **[John 4:43-50](/bible/john/4#v43)** *[[3:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=185s)]* > [43](/bible/john/4#v43) Now after two days he departed thence, and went into Galilee. > > [44](/bible/john/4#v44) For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honour in his own country. > > [45](/bible/john/4#v45) Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast. > > [46](/bible/john/4#v46) So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum. > > [47](/bible/john/4#v47) When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death. > > [48](/bible/john/4#v48) Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe. > > [49](/bible/john/4#v49) The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die. > > [50](/bible/john/4#v50) Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way. - Jesus himself testified that a prophet hath no honour in his own country. Because why? Christ was from the region of Galilee. That's where he grew up, in Nazareth. - The Galileans received him, having seen all the things he did at Jerusalem at the feast: these Galileans were in Jerusalem, and they witnessed the miracles that he did. - Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine: this is where Christ was doing some of his first miracles. Turning water to wine, off the top right there, should have had everybody repenting. Especially the negro, especially the Israelite. This negro just turned water to wine. - Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe. This is something that Christ understood about his people. Man, we have got to see signs and wonders; we have got to have extravagant things happen for us to believe. **[John 4:52-54](/bible/john/4#v52)** *[[5:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=338s)]* > [52](/bible/john/4#v52) Then enquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him. > > [53](/bible/john/4#v53) So the father knew that it was at the same hour, in the which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house. > > [54](/bible/john/4#v54) This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judea into Galilee. - His son started to be healed at the same hour Jesus said unto him, thy son liveth. - This is again the second miracle that Jesus did. So here in this region of Galilee, Christ was doing many miracles: turning water to wine, healing the nobleman's son. These are the acts that were going on around this time.
Reading from an article from Holy Land Site, on screen *[[6:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=383s)]* > Holy Land Site. Bringing the Bible to life by seeing where it took place. > Historical background. Chorazin was one of the three towns, Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum, that made up what scholars call the Evangelical Triangle. - You see that? This is the Evangelical Triangle right here. These are the three cities that the Lord cursed. > Jesus set up his home ministry base in Capernaum, which was close to Chorazin. Jesus spent around 65% of his ministry time around the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee. So those of Chorazin would have repeatedly heard and seen - They would have repeatedly heard and seen all that Jesus did, all the miracles. So the Lord said, these miracles that I did amongst you, if I had done them in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented. If I had done it in Sodom, I wouldn't even have destroyed it; it would still be here right now, because I did a lot of miracles here. He was going back and forth in this triangle through these three cities. > A tree with a kind of thorns that would have been used for the crown of thorns Jesus wore at his crucifixion can be found here.
**[Mark 1:21-28](/bible/mark/1#v21)** *[[7:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=473s)]* > [21](/bible/mark/1#v21) And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught. > > [22](/bible/mark/1#v22) And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes. > > [23](/bible/mark/1#v23) And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out, > > [24](/bible/mark/1#v24) Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God. > > [25](/bible/mark/1#v25) And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. > > [26](/bible/mark/1#v26) And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him. > > [27](/bible/mark/1#v27) And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him. > > [28](/bible/mark/1#v28) And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee. - Familiarity. Here he is in the synagogue in Capernaum, about to heal this man with an unclean spirit, saying, what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? - The unclean spirit was able to identify him: this is the son of man. But the negroes around him, because of familiarity, couldn't see it. - Can you imagine that? This man tormented, the unclean spirit saying, I know you, Jesus of Nazareth, and Christ responds, hold your peace and come out of him. That would have tore some people up. Seeing that should have changed minds right there. - With authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him: this dude is talking to the unclean spirits with all authority, and they're obeying him. - Immediately his fame spread abroad. So everybody knew. Everybody understood: Christ is going around healing folks, turning water to wine, talking to the unclean spirits, and they're obeying him. **[Matthew 4:23-25](/bible/matthew/4#v23)** *[[10:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=617s)]* > [23](/bible/matthew/4#v23) And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. > > [24](/bible/matthew/4#v24) And his fame went throughout all Syria: and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatick, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them. > > [25](/bible/matthew/4#v25) And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judea, and from beyond Jordan. - Jesus went about all Galilee: we're still in those regions. - His fame went throughout all Syria, and they brought unto him all sick people: after people heard, they brought the sick and the diseased, and he healed a lot of people. Everybody understood what was going on in this region, in Galilee. - There followed him great multitudes of people. Galilee was a region, a district if you will, in northern Israel, and these are the three cities he would make rounds and rotation through, teaching in the synagogues. **[Isaiah 9:1-2](/bible/isaiah/9#v1)** *[[11:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=703s)]* > [1](/bible/isaiah/9#v1) Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations. > > [2](/bible/isaiah/9#v2) The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined. - It was prophesied this was going to happen. Nazareth was the place where he was raised; remember, he was born in Bethlehem. - Galilee of the nations: he had the afflicted people in this region. - The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: it was prophesied that they were going to see a great light, that they were going to see Christ, hear of Christ. - Upon them hath the light shined. This was always prophesied: Christ was going to be doing a lot of miracles in this region. **[John 7:40-41](/bible/john/7#v40)** *[[12:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=774s)]* > [40](/bible/john/7#v40) Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the Prophet. > > [41](/bible/john/7#v41) Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, Shall Christ come out of Galilee? - What's interesting is that people looked down on the region itself, even though it was prophesied that they were going to see a great light. - Shall Christ come out of Galilee? Shall Christ come out of the ghetto? That was the notion of a lot of people. **[John 1:45-46](/bible/john/1#v45)** *[[13:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=821s)]* > [45](/bible/john/1#v45) Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph. > > [46](/bible/john/1#v46) And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see. - We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth: he's from that region, he's doing many miracles. We found this guy. Why? Because we heard of him, the fame, the miracles. - Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Everybody was looking down upon the region: can any good thing come out of the ghettos of Nazareth? - Familiarity breeds death. - Come and see: man, come find out for yourself. Don't allow your familiarity. Don't think that because it's in the regions where it's just ghettos and debauchery, a prophet can't rise up out of there. Come see for yourself. **[John 7:41-52](/bible/john/7#v41)** *[[15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=900s)]* > [41](/bible/john/7#v41) Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, Shall Christ come out of Galilee? > > [42](/bible/john/7#v42) Hath not the scripture said, That Christ cometh of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was? > > [43](/bible/john/7#v43) So there was a division among the people because of him. > > [44](/bible/john/7#v44) And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him. > > [45](/bible/john/7#v45) Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him? > > [46](/bible/john/7#v46) The officers answered, Never man spake like this man. > > [47](/bible/john/7#v47) Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived? > > [48](/bible/john/7#v48) Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him? > > [49](/bible/john/7#v49) But this people who knoweth not the law are cursed. > > [50](/bible/john/7#v50) Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, being one of them,) > > [51](/bible/john/7#v51) Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth? > > [52](/bible/john/7#v52) They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet. - Hath not the scripture said that Christ cometh of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem? So there was a division amongst them. They were confused: we read the scripture, he's supposed to come out of Bethlehem, but he's coming out of Galilee. And we know these negroes in Galilee, we know these negroes in the ghetto. Ain't nothing good coming out of there. Familiarity. - This people who knoweth not the law are cursed: here you have the leaders, the ones that rejected, and their minions saying, listen, y'all don't know the laws; that's the only reason you're following that Christ, because you don't know the scriptures. Don't that sound familiar? Things that make you go hmm. - Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet. Look at the scriptures, search and look: ain't no damn prophets been prophesied to come out of Galilee. But they were deceived, because Isaiah already told them they were going to see a great light. Blinded. - So that familiarity, guess what it bred in them? Death. **[Matthew 21:10-12](/bible/matthew/21#v10)** *[[17:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1053s)]* > [10](/bible/matthew/21#v10) And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this? > > [11](/bible/matthew/21#v11) And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee. > > [12](/bible/matthew/21#v12) And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves, - This is those of Jerusalem: who is this? This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee. - Those who didn't see his upbringing, dwelling in a whole other region in Jerusalem, acknowledged it quick: hey, that's Jesus of Nazareth, this is that prophet. **[Mark 6:1-6](/bible/mark/6#v1)** *[[18:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1093s)]* > [1](/bible/mark/6#v1) And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him. > > [2](/bible/mark/6#v2) And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands? > > [3](/bible/mark/6#v3) Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him. > > [4](/bible/mark/6#v4) But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. > > [5](/bible/mark/6#v5) And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. > > [6](/bible/mark/6#v6) And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching. - You had people that weren't from the region, and they acknowledged it. But what was the mindset of those who grew up with him? - Is not this the carpenter? Ain't that the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James? And they were offended at him. We know this young brother. We know his parents. We know his sisters. How dare you come and try to take our place? How dare you come and start teaching the word of God? We know you. - Don't this sound familiar? This is why I said this class is for you young brothers and sisters. Yes, y'all are repenting. You have got family looking at you crazy, friends looking at you crazy, that don't want to listen to you. They are seeing Christ within you. And that rejection is of old. That familiarity is of old. - A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country: he goes outside to Jerusalem, and they acknowledge it quick. Those in Galilee question: oh no, we know his daddy, we know his mama, we know his upbringing. The spirit of the Lord ain't on that man. Who do you think you are? - He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk: you wonder why only a couple people repent, only a couple people are listening in your family? He said it was only a few people he could help. - He marvelled because of their unbelief, and he went round about the villages, teaching: that didn't discourage him from teaching. He just marvelled at the unbelief based off of familiarity. - So in these last days, a lot of people are going to reject this truth solely because of familiarity, solely because of what they think they know of you, of the Christ within you.
Reading from a definition of familiarity breeds contempt, on screen *[[21:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1277s)]* > Familiarity breeds contempt is a well-known proverb meaning that close, long-term contact with a person, place, or situation can cause you to lose respect, lose appreciation, or take them for granted. - Not only is this going to affect those who watched you grow up; it's going to affect those in the body. That familiarity is going to start to breed contempt, to have you losing respect because of the long-term contact. - There's a lot of people in the world, I'm telling you, that are not going to get this truth in Babylon because they're familiar with your upbringing, familiar with you, and they don't want to acknowledge that spirit within you, that spirit of Christ.
**[1 Samuel 10:9-12](/bible/1-samuel/10#v9)** *[[22:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1339s)]* > [9](/bible/1-samuel/10#v9) And it was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day. > > [10](/bible/1-samuel/10#v10) And when they came thither to the hill, behold, a company of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them. > > [11](/bible/1-samuel/10#v11) And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets? > > [12](/bible/1-samuel/10#v12) And one of the same place answered and said, But who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets? - Talking about the death from familiarity. God gave him another heart: God gave Saul another mind. - When all that knew him beforetime saw that he prophesied among the prophets: what is this that is come unto the son of Kish? What the hell came upon the son of Kish? We knew this dude before time. We know your daddy. - Is Saul also among the prophets? Is he out there standing with the purple and gold? Who do you think you are? - We think this is a new spirit. No, this familiarity is of old right here, and a lot of people are going to get caught up in this thing.
Reading from a commentary on "but who is their father?" (1 Samuel 10:12) from Bible Hub, on screen *[[24:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1441s)]* > And who is their father? This rhetorical question suggests doubt about the legitimacy or origin of the prophetic group Saul was seen with. In ancient Israel, lineage and family background were significant, often determining one's social and religious roles. The question implies skepticism about the authority or authenticity of the prophets - Because of the upbringing, now you're questioning the authenticity of the prophets. Are these the prophets? Who's your father? Who's your upbringing? Who is your teacher? > and by extension, Saul's sudden inclusion among them. - How the hell did you get included among them? So we're questioning you. > It underscores the theme that God's choices often defy human expectations and societal norms. - You see that? Remember the scripture says his works among men are hidden.
**[John 3:8](/bible/john/3#v8)** *[[25:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1513s)]* > [8](/bible/john/3#v8) The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit. - The wind bloweth where it listeth, but you don't know where the hell it's coming from, or where it's going. - So is every one that is born of the Spirit: all you see is the results. All you see is trees falling. That's how the spirit moves. The spirit hits a brother, and all of a sudden now he's prophesying. You just see the results. - But people don't understand this, and a lot of people are going to get put to death.
Reading from a second commentary on "who is their father?" (1 Samuel 10:12), on screen *[[25:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1558s)]* > As an instance of the extreme surprise with which the association of Saul with the sons of the prophets was witnessed by the inhabitants of Gibeah, an association apparently very foreign to his old habits - It was foreign to his old habits. They couldn't distinguish the two. We've been knowing this guy. We know his father Kish. We know his upbringing. How are you among the prophets? > and to the manner of life of his family. - We know your family. A lot of us come from debauched families, hoodwinked families, economically based families. Now all of a sudden you're preaching, you're prophesying, you're on the streets teaching. We know your family. > A short dialogue between two of the citizens of Gibeah is here related, a conversation important owing to the words uttered by the second citizen in reply to the amazed question, What is this that has come unto the son of Kish? The reply gives us some insight into the deep conviction entertained by the ordinary Israelite of the days of Samuel that the invisible God was ever present. > > The reply of the second citizen has been well explained by Von Bunsen. Is the son of Kish then a prophet? asked the first citizen, surprised apparently that one … so unlikely to train up a son of the prophets - Ain't no way. We know your father. He was a drug dealer, a whoremonger. We know this, and we know he ain't imputed no damn wisdom in you. Now you want to call yourself a prophet? > should have a son associated in this peculiar and sudden manner with a chosen band of scholars and teachers. - You know, one day you're drinking, you're smoking, you're clubbing, then the next week here you are riding on the street and holding post. What is the change? > To this question the second citizen replied, no doubt pointing to the … group from the prophet schools of Gibeah, Do you wonder that the son of so rough and uncultivated a man as Kish receive the divine gift which we all love so well and admire so greatly? - You know, when the brothers break it down to the scriptures, you're in awe. How you know this precept? How you know that precept? Damn, he's answering every question with precepts, precepts, precepts. But wait a minute, I know that guy. I know your father, and nothing good came from your family. And now all of a sudden you're there with the prophets? Death by familiarity.
**[1 Corinthians 4:9-14](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v9)** *[[29:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwBHD-OIrsg&t=1761s)]* > [9](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v9) For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men. > > [10](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v10) We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised. > > [11](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v11) Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace; > > [12](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v12) And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it: > > [13](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v13) Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day. > > [14](/bible/1-corinthians/4#v14) I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you. - God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death, for we are made a spectacle unto the world. - We are fools for Christ's sake, but ye are wise in Christ: talking about those in the world, those leaders. Ye are honourable, but we are despised. You can relate that: you've got Christianity and you've got the prophets. Christianity, they're raised up, they're honourable, they're strong.
